author: Bobby Grayson
description: elixir/to_lean.exs: defers = loop modules with no clause where guard == nil and bare?(mpat). render_clauses/2 tags each rendered clause with its module, finds the module's last clause index and appends defer_clause(ctx, mod) right after it; the module ctor is then added to ctx.covered so no global catch-all is emitted (Gen/Supervisor.lean lost '| _, _, s, _ => (s, [])'). loop_tail/2 recurses into {:if, ..} and {:case, ..} branches; on a block it splits off the last statement: {^fname, _, [e]} -> {:noreply, e}; {:exit, _, [_]} kept; otherwise value?(last) (atom/int/list/var/tuple) drops the value and appends exit(:normal), a non-value statement is kept and followed by exit(:normal). Why it matters: this is the encoding of selective receive; the re-enqueue delivers to self, so the message count of the process is preserved and the proof must frame it (mcount_deliver). The explorer never sends start/EXIT to a worker, so the defer clause does not enlarge the explored state space; it is exercised by beh_eq_gen and the SupervisorProof cases, not by the checker.
title: Defer clause and loop_tail semantics: a loop module with no unguarded bare-pattern clause gets '| me, _, .<mod> s_0.., m => (.<mod> s_0.., [.send me m])' after its last clause; tail 'f(e)' -> {:noreply, e}, 'exit(r)' kept, statement kept then exit(:normal), plain value -> exit(:normal); rewriting descends through if/case
